at_running_time_ms.description: Programme running time to open the break on. Omit to roll now.

return_to.description: Source to rejoin afterwards. Omit to return to whatever is on air.

uri.description: File path or URI of the clip to roll.

AdStatus.description: An ad break, either armed for a future cue or currently on air.

on_air.description: False while it is prerolled and waiting for its cue.

return_to.description: Source to return to when the ad ends. None returns to the slate.

AddDestinationRequest.description: `channel.destination.add`. Send a channel's stream on to a platform.

id.description: The channel.

key.description: The stream key. Write only: no method reads it back.

label.description: What the list calls it. The platform's name when left out.

platform.description: youtube, facebook, twitch, custom or srt.

rendition.description:
Convert the stream before sending it: `{"preset": "youtube-720p30"}`
or a rendition request written out. Left out, or one the stream
already matches, the stream is sent as it arrives.

server.description:
The ingest address. Left out, the platform's own; custom and srt need
one.

stream.description:
Which of the channel's streams to send. `*`, the default, is the first
one live.

id.description: The name this filter answers to afterwards. A slug, and yours to pick.

params.description:
The filter's own settings. What goes in here is the filter's business,
not the core's.

programme.description: Filter the programme rather than one source.

side.description:
`input` puts it before the proxy boundary, where the thumbnail sees it
too; `programme` puts it on this source's programme branch only.

source.description:
The source to hang it on. Leave it out and set `programme` to filter
everything that goes out.

type.description: A filter type id, as `plugin.list` and `core.api` `kinds` report them.
A filter type id, as `plugin.list` reports them.

content.description:
What the item shows: `{"source": "cam1"}`, `{"ref": "<scene id>"}` or
`{"graphic": "plugin/id"}`.

draft.description:
A draft id from `scene.edit.begin`, to change a working copy instead of
the live document.

enter.description:
How it comes in and goes out when shown or hidden on air:
`{type, edge, duration_ms, easing, on_take}`, as on `scene.item.set`.

name.description:
What to call it. Left out, a source item is named after its source,
because a model reasons about words.

transform.description:
Where it goes. Left out, the next free cell of a grid over what is
already there, so a drop on a scene never needs a dialog.

visible.description:
`false` adds it hidden, so a graphic can be put on a scene that is on
air and shown later with its `enter`. Left out, it is shown.

AddOutputRequest.description:
`output.add`. The id and the URL are the whole of it for an RTMP
destination; anything else a kind understands rides in `params`.

id.description: Stable id for this destination.

policy.description:
Reconnect policy: "own" retries quickly, for servers you run; "cdn"
backs off harder, for platforms that penalise hammering.

rendition.description:
What to make from the programme for this destination: a rendition
request or `{"preset": "youtube-720p30"}` (`rendition.presets` lists
them). Absent means the programme encoder, at no extra cost.

uri.description:
rtmp:// or rtmps:// URL including the stream key. Left out for a
kind with no address of its own, such as `hls/output`, which is
served from the control port.

source.description:
Where the plugin comes from. One of: `owner/repo` (a GitHub release,
optionally `@version`), a git URL ending in `.git`, `cargo:name`,
`npm:@scope/name`, `pypi:name`, `oci:ref`, an absolute path to a
directory, or a bare plugin name to look up in the marketplaces.

color.description: A colour for every client, the tally and the Stream Deck to agree on.

id.description:
Stable id used by `program.take` and `source.remove`. Lowercase
letters, digits and dashes. Derived from the name or the host when
omitted, with a numeric suffix if that is taken.

kind.description:
"web" renders the URL as a page in the browser sidecar, the same as
writing `web+` in front of it. "auto" or omitted works the protocol out
from the URL.

name.description: Name shown to an operator. Defaults to the host of the URL.

superimpose.description:
Websites only: "auto" lets the mixer decode the page's own video
outside the browser and draw the page over the top, which saves about a
CPU core. "off" is the default.

uri.description: Stream URL, file path, or with kind "web" the address of a page.

black.description: Fraction of the picture at black. Default 0.98.

freeze_ms.description: How long the picture has to be identical. Default 200.

silence_ms.description: How long the programme has to be quiet. Default 500.

AgentExt.description: `ext.agent`. `true` takes the default thresholds; an object moves them.

detail.description: One sentence for a person: what was measured, and against what.

since_ms.description:
Unix milliseconds when the condition began. For black, freeze and
silence that is when the picture or sound first measured so, not when
the alarm's duration ran out.

AlarmSettings.description:
A show's alarms, as a person sets them from the page. Left out fields
keep the measuring side's defaults; a duration of 0 switches that check
off.

enabled.description:
Whether black, freeze and silence are watched at all. Left out: on
for a show without compositing, off for one that composites.

silence_dbfs.description: The peak level under which sound counts as quiet.

Align.description: The nine alignment keywords, used to place content inside its frame.

Applies.description: When a change to a key takes effect.

oneOf.description: In force as soon as `config.set` answers.
Used by every source added or rebuilt after the change.
Written to the file and used from the next start.

frame.description: Answer with a still of the armed scene as well as the records.

item.description:
Which placement, by the name you gave the item or by its id. Left out,
every placement of this graphic is filled.

play.description: Bring it on after filling it in.

values.description: The fields, by name. `scene.item.schema` says which there are.

duration_ms.description: How long the change takes, in milliseconds. 0 is a cut.

scene.description:
The scene to apply it to. Left out, a new one is made. Applying onto an
existing scene keeps the item ids, so an animated layout change is a
property ramp rather than a cut.

values.description: The layout's parameters by name: its source slots and its numbers.

dry_run.description: Work out the plan and write nothing.

force.description: Take the preset's value wherever the operator already has one.

keep_sources.description: Leave the operator's sources and outputs alone.

name.description: A preset name, or a path to a directory holding `gmx-plugin.toml`.

applied.description: Present when the preset was actually applied.

dry_run.description: True when nothing was written because `dry_run` was set.

live.description: The sources and outputs this core picked up without a restart.

needs_restart.description: What still needs a restart, in plain words. Empty is the good case.

plan.description: The whole plan, as JSON. The same object `preset.list` rows point at.

Asset.description: A file the collection carries with it.

path.description: Relative to the collection root, always.

Audio.description:
Whether the item's source is heard. A source is audible when any live item
of it says so, which is OBS's behaviour and changes no pad topology.

oneOf.description: Heard while the item is visible on programme.
Heard whether the item is visible or not.
Never heard.

AudioSetParams.description:
`source.audio.set` takes an id as well as the levels: the id comes off the
path on REST and out of the params on `/rpc`, and both land in one object.

gain.description:
The operator's fader for the whole source, 0.0 to 10.0. Omit to leave
it where it is.

id.description: Source id.

media.description:
Gain per video underneath, by position. A null entry, or a list shorter
than the number of videos, leaves those alone: `[null, 0.0]` silences
the second video and touches nothing else.

muted.description:
Mute the whole source. Held apart from the fader, so unmuting comes
back to the level that was set.

page.description: Gain on a superimposed page's own sound.

AudioWant.description: The audio an output wants. Every field left out is taken from the source.

BackupInput.description: An input's backup: an input with no backup of its own.

param.description:
An expression over the collection's params and `W`, `H`. An empty
string takes the binding off.

prop.description: A geometry path such as `frame.w` or `position.x`.

BindingAddRequest.description: `feed.binding.add`: the fields of [`BindingSpec`], with anything else refused.

id.description: A slug. Never changes. Made from the target when absent.

select.description: A path into the fetched document. See [`BindingSpec`].

join.description: An empty string takes the join away.

template.description: An empty string takes the template away.

BindingStatus.description: A binding with what it last wrote.

id.description: A slug. Never changes.

join.description: For a list: join it into one string with this between the elements.

limit.description: For a list: keep the first this many.

select.description:
A path into the fetched document: `items[].title`, `data.home.score`,
`rows[0].Name`, or a JSON pointer starting `/`. Empty is the whole
document. `[]` takes every element of a list.

template.description:
Words with `{path}` holes filled from what `select` picked (from each
element, for a list): `{home} {home_score} : {away_score} {away}`.

writes.description: Writes since the core started. A feed that has not changed adds none.

anyOf.description:
A source's param through `source.set`, by a dotted path that starts
at `params`: `params.text`, `params.items`, `params.fields.headline`.

A field of an OGraf graphic on a scene, through `scene.apply_graphic`
with no play, which is the graphic's update action.

item.description: The item's name, when the graphic is on the canvas twice.

anyOf.description:
A scene parameter through `scene.params.set`, so every `{{name}}`
in the collection follows it.

BindingTarget.description: Where a binding writes. One of three shapes.

Blend.description: OBS's blend enum, so an import carries across unchanged.

BridgeTransport.description: How media crosses between a node and the core.

oneOf.description:
RTP over UDP with RFC 6051 header extensions. The default: the receiver
knows the sender's timeline from the first packet.
SRT, for a link that loses packets. ARQ without inventing anything.
WHIP, for a WAN or a NAT nobody controls.

BulkPlan.description: What a batch costs, priced by the governor without taking anything.

assumed_input.description:
The input every rendition was priced against, because an input's
shape is known only once it arrives.

cost.description: Every rendition of the shows that fit, summed. Copies cost nothing.

fits.description: Whether every show of the batch fits.

have.description: What the machine has free now.

Bundle.description: What an importer is told before it reads the document.

assets.description: Every file carried, by the path inside the bundle.

id.description:
The collection's own stable id, repeated here so a listing can be read
without unpacking the document.

requires.description:
Every plugin this collection needs, with the version range that will
do. An importer that has none of them still gets the geometry.

skipped.description:
What could not be carried, one line each, so a partial export is
visible rather than silent.

written_by.description: The build that wrote it, for a bug report.

BundleAsset.description: One file carried in the bundle.

id.description: The asset id in the document.

path.description:
Relative to the bundle root, forward slashes. Never absolute: see the
head of this module.

confirm.description:
Measure even though something is on air. The measurement takes a few
seconds of every core and can cost what is on air frames.

Canvas.description:
The output raster. One per collection in this release; 11 section 1 leaves
room for several.

CanvasInfo.description: The canvas every source is scaled onto and every output leaves by.

source.description: None means this cell is the program return.

names.description:
Host names and addresses it is for. Defaults to this machine's
address, `localhost` and `127.0.0.1`.

CertificateInfo.description: The certificate RTMPS answers with. The private key never leaves the core.

created.description: When it was set, RFC 3339 in UTC.

fingerprint.description:
SHA-256 of the certificate, as colon separated hex, to compare with
what an encoder shows.

names.description: The names it was made for, for a self signed one.

source.description: `uploaded`, or `self_signed` for one the mixer made.

cert.description: The certificate, and any chain after it, as PEM.

Change.description: One thing an import does or would do.

id.description: The id, key, scene name or clip name, as the file has it.

to.description: The new id or name, for a rename.

Channel.description: A named place encoders publish to, over every protocol it has switched on.

app.description: The RTMP application name: the path segment after the port.

auto_source.description: A stream that goes live becomes a mixer source by itself.

destinations.description:
Where the channel's streams are sent on to, with what each is doing.
Changed by `channel.destination.*`.

enabled.description: Off turns every publisher away with a sentence saying so.

keys.description: The keys as hints, never the key itself: a read token sees only these.

name.description: What a person calls it.

protocols.description: The protocols it takes publishers over, besides RTMPS.

rtmps.description: RTMPS, on a port of its own, when a person has turned it on.

streams.description:
Live streams, and streams that left while a scene still holds their
source.

app.description: Defaults to a slug of the name.

ChannelAdded.description: What `channel.add` answers: the channel and its first key.

ChannelKey.description: One key, as a list shows it.

created.description: When it was made, RFC 3339 in UTC.

hint.description: The last four characters, so a person can tell two keys apart.

certificate.description: The certificate RTMPS answers with, when there is one.

hosts.description: The addresses an encoder can reach this machine at, first one first.

listeners.description:
Every listener a channel needs, open or not, and why: the ports this
mixer has open for ingest, and the channels each is open for.

ChannelProtocol.description:
A way a publisher reaches a channel. RTMPS is `Rtmps`, set apart
because it has a port of its own.

oneOf.description: `rtmp://<host>:<rtmp port>/<app>/<stream>?psk=<key>`.

`srt://<host>:<srt port>?streamid=<app>/<stream>`, the key as the
passphrase or as `?psk=` in the stream id.

`POST http://<host>:<control port>/whip/<app>/<stream>`, the key as
the bearer token.

addresses.description: The same for every protocol the channel has on, RTMP first.

example.description: `<server>/main?psk=<key>`, with `<key>` left for the person to fill.

protocols.description: Which protocols it takes, as a whole list: `["rtmp", "srt"]`.

rtmps.description: RTMPS on or off, and its port.

dropped_gops.description: Whole GOPs readers of it have lost by falling behind, this session.

key.description: The id of the key that let it in.

relay.description:
Where a mixer on this machine reads it: the listener's own port on
loopback. Any show adds it as a source with `source.add {type:
"ingest/rtmp", relay, stream: "<app>/<name>"}`, and every show that
does reads the one stream the station received.

since_ms.description: When it last went live, in milliseconds since 1970.

source.description: The mixer source it feeds, when it feeds one.

state.description: `live`, or `idle` for one that left while a scene holds its source.

ConfigChanged.description: One key this call changed, and when the change takes effect.

note.description: Said when something outside the file wins over it, such as `--bind`.

keys.description: Only these dotted keys. Empty or absent is every key.

needs_restart.description: Every key whose new value waits for a restart, whichever keys were asked for.

path.description: The config file these values are read from and written to.

overridden_by.description:
What wins over the file for this key, when something does: `--bind`,
or `GODWINMIX_TOKEN` in the core's environment.

pending.description:
True when the file differs from what the running core uses and only a
restart will close the gap.

set.description: For a secret: whether one is set. The value itself is never sent.

source.description: `file` when the key is written in the config file, `default` when not.

value.description:
What the config file says, or the default when it says nothing. Always
null for a secret.

keys.description: Dotted keys to take out of the config file, so their defaults apply.

values.description:
Dotted key to new value: `{"program.video_bitrate_kbps": 4500}`. Null
puts a key back to its default. For a secret, the sentinel
`"__secret__"` means leave it as it is, and an empty string clears it.

applied.description: Keys from this call in force now.

changed.description: Every key this call changed, each with its `applies`.

dry_run.description: True when nothing was written because `dry_run` was set.

needs_restart.description:
Every key, from this call or an earlier one, whose new value waits for
a restart. Empty is the good case.

next_source.description: Keys from this call every source added or rebuilt from now on uses.

unchanged.description: Secrets sent back as the sentinel, so left as they were.

Container.description:
How the bytes leave. Decides which codecs are allowed: FLV carries H.264
(and HEVC and AV1 in enhanced RTMP), WebRTC wants VP8, VP9, H.264 or AV1.

ConversionState.description: One conversion, in flight or remembered after it finished.

error.description:
Set only on `failed`, shown to the operator verbatim: "no AAC encoder
available" is worth more than "conversion failed".

progress.description: 0.0 to 1.0, position over duration, both read off the pipeline.

CoreInfo.description: `core.info`: what this core is, what it can do, and where its edges are.

features.description:
Feature strings a client can branch on: multiview, snapshot, uploads,
mcp, browser, exec-sources, rehearsal, tokens.

rehearsal.description:
True when the core was started with `--rehearsal`, which refuses
`output.add` and accepts rehearsal tokens.

restart.description:
Whether `core.restart` brings this core back, so a page can decide
between a Restart button and a sentence.

supervised.description:
True when the core was started with `--supervised` (or
`GODWINMIX_SUPERVISED=1`): a service manager, a container runtime or
the desktop app starts it again after it exits.

tls.description:
HTTPS on the control port, when it is on. Absent when `[control.tls]`
is off or the certificate could not be loaded.

token.description: Present when the request carried a token the core recognises.

ui.description:
What a surface should start with, when a preset chose it. Absent on a
core no preset has been applied to, which is what puts the welcome
panel up in the reference UI.

version.description: The build's own version, as in Cargo.toml.

Cost.description: What running one piece of work costs, in units the governor adds up.

cpu_millicores.description: Thousandths of one CPU core. 1000 is one whole core.

device_millis.description:
Share of one hardware device, in thousandths of what it can do, when
the work runs on one.

device_sessions.description: Hardware encoder sessions held (consumer NVIDIA cards cap these).

egress_kbps.description: Bytes per second out of the machine, in kbit/s.

memory_mib.description: Resident memory the work adds, in MiB.

measured_millicores.description:
What a station's processes cost now, read when asked: its own, every
show process and every plugin it started. Left out by a single
process core and where another process's CPU cannot be read.

CreateFromAnswer.description: The scene `scene.create_from` made, and what it did on the way.

added.description: Sources this call added for files it was given.

findings.description:
What `scene.validate` would say about it, so a client shows a warning
without asking again.

geometry.description:
Where each item actually lands, after groups are flattened and
references resolved. Bottom of the stack first, which is the order the
compositor takes them in.

key.description:
For a keyed layout, the colour written on the key: "#rrggbb", or
"auto" when no still of the camera could be had.

records.description: The scene's own record and one per item, parents before children.

layout.description:
A layout name from `scene.layout.list`. Left out, the number of sources
picks one.

settings.description:
Values for the layout's own settings, by name, as `scene.layout.list`
lists them: for `virtual-set`, `key` ("auto" or "#rrggbb"),
`presenter_scale` and `presenter_x`. A keyed layout with no `key`
guesses the colour from the camera. `screen` says what is behind the
presenter: "green" (the default), "blue", or "none", which cuts the
person out with a model and needs no screen at all.

sources.description:
What to lay out, in slot order. Each is a source id, a file name from
the media library, or a path or URL to a picture or clip; a file becomes
a source the first time and is reused after that.

Crop.description:
How much of the content's own pixels to trim, normalised 0 to 1 so it
survives a canvas change. vMix and CasparCG do this; OBS crops in pixels,
which is why an OBS collection moved from 1080p to 720p loses its crops.

Destination.description:
One destination as a client sees it. The key never appears: `has_key`
says whether there is one.

error.description: What went wrong last, in words a person can act on.

id.description: A slug, unique within its channel: `youtube`, `youtube-2`.

kbps.description: What is going out, over the last second.

plan.description: What the plan gave it, while its stream is live.

platform.description: A platform id from the table: youtube, facebook, twitch, custom, srt.

playback.description: Where a player opens it, for an output this machine serves as HLS.

reconnects.description: Connections lost and made again since it was switched on.

refused.description: Why it is not sending what it asked for, and what would fit.

rendition.description: What it asked to be converted to. Absent: sent as it arrives.

stream.description: Which of the channel's streams to send. `*` is the first live one.

uri_host.description: The scheme, host and port, and nothing that could carry a key.

DestinationMode.description: Copied as it arrives, or converted.

DestinationPlan.description: The plan's answer for one destination.

encoder.description:
The video encoder, `h264-videotoolbox`, and why that one. Absent for a
copy.

nodes.description:
The plan's nodes this destination reads, so a page can show which
work it shares with the channel's other destinations.

reason.description:
One sentence: "copied: the source's video goes out as it is", "encoded
because the source is 1920x1080 and this output wants 1280x720".

stream.description: The stream it was planned against, when the destination names `*`.

DestinationRefusal.description:
Why a destination that asked for a rendition is not sending, and what
would. `error` on the destination carries the same sentence.

advice.description: Renditions that would fit now, largest first.

code.description:
`governor` (the machine has no room), `plan` (nothing here can make
it), `shed` (it ran and was stopped to keep what is on air).

DestinationState.description: Where a destination has got to.

oneOf.description: Switched off by the person.
Switched on, and waiting for the stream it sends to go live.
Dialling the far end for the first time.
Sending.
Lost the far end and dialling it again on the backoff.

The far end said no in a way retrying will not fix: the key was
refused. `error` says what to change.

DeviceTotal.description: Use of one hardware device by a plan.

sessions_max.description: Absent when the device showed no limit.

timeout_ms.description:
How long to look, shared between the devices. Two seconds by default,
four and a half at most, because no method blocks for five.

How long to listen. Capped at 4.5 seconds, so the call stays inside the
five second ceiling every method is held to.

draft.description: Pass this as `draft` on any `scene.item.*` call to edit the copy.

live.description: True when the client asked to edit on air.

scene.description: The scene it was taken from.

view.description: The scene as it stands, so the client has something to draw at once.

name.description: What to call the copy. A name already in use gets a number after it.

id.description: The source to copy.

name.description: Name for the copy. The original's name and " copy" when omitted.

new_id.description:
Id for the copy. Derived from its name when omitted, with a numeric
suffix if that is taken.

live.description:
True to edit the scene that is on air as you go. The default is off
air: the draft is applied on the next take or on an explicit apply.

address.description:
Where the node is, for the record. The node always dials the core, so
this is what `node.list` shows before it has.

name.description:
What the node will call itself. A slug: it goes in `place` and in the
node's certificate.

ttl_secs.description: How long the token is good for. Default one hour.

ErrorAction.description:
One thing a client can offer as a button. `label` is the button's text,
`kind` says what pressing it does, and the other fields are the ones that
kind uses. Flat rather than an enum with data, so every generated client
reads every field.

applies.description:
`set-config`: what `config.get` says about the key: `live`,
`next_source` or `restart`.

command.description:
A command the person runs themselves, for what only the operating
system can supply. A client shows it with a copy button, beside the
action's own button when the kind is not `copy`.

key.description: `set-config`: the dotted key. `open`: the setting to show.

label.description: Short, in the imperative, for a person: "Turn the multiview on".

Put the clips themselves in, as base64, rather than their names and
sizes. Refused past 256 MB: copy the media folder instead.

Put stream keys, channel keys, destination addresses and the control
token in the file. Off unless asked; admin scope either way.

page.description:
Whatever the page wants back when the file is opened: its layout and
its settings. Carried as it is.

`json` for the document alone, `zip` for a bundle with its assets, or
`dir` for the same bundle unpacked.

`dir`. For `zip`, leaving it out hands the bytes back as base64.

declines multiview; a Stream Deck takes tally only; an agent takes nothing.

or `"full"` for a full resolution preview compositor built while
subscribed. See 11 section 3.

id.description: A slug: lower case letters, digits and dashes. Never changes.

interval_s.description: Seconds between fetches of a polled feed. At least 5; 30 when absent.

timeout_s.description: Seconds one fetch may take. 10 when absent.

FeedFormat.description:
How the body is read. `auto` decides from the content type and the first
byte; `sse` reads an `http(s)` address as a Server-Sent Events stream.

oneOf.description: RSS 2.0 or Atom, read as `{title, link, items: [{title, link, summary, published, id, author}]}`.
Comma separated with a header row, read as `{columns, rows: [{column: value}]}`.
Plain text, read as `{text, lines}`.
Server-Sent Events: each event's `data` is one document.

headers.description: Replaces the headers. A value of `"__secret__"` keeps what is stored.

oneOf.description: Not fetched yet, or connecting.
The last fetch, message or event was read.
The last attempt failed; it is tried again with a growing gap.

FeedStatus.description: A feed with what it has been doing.

bytes.description: Size of the last body read, in bytes.

failures.description: Attempts in a row that failed.

fetches.description: Fetches or messages read since the core started.

headers.description:
Sent with every request, for an API key. Sealed once stored: read
back as `"__secret__"`, and `"__secret__"` written back keeps it.

id.description: A slug: lower case letters, digits and dashes. Never changes.

interval_s.description:
Seconds between fetches of a polled feed. At least 5; 30 when absent.
Not used by a websocket or an event stream, which push.

last_change.description: When what was read last differed from what came before.

last_fetch.description: When something was last read, RFC 3339.

not_modified.description: Fetches the server answered `304 Not Modified`.

paused.description: Stopped by `feed.pause`: nothing is fetched and nothing is written.

timeout_s.description: Seconds one fetch may take before it counts as failed. 10 when absent.

FeedTestRequest.description:
`feed.test`: fetch once and show what a selection picks.

Give `id` for a feed that exists, or `address` (with `format`, `headers`
and `timeout_s` if it needs them) for one that does not yet. Nothing is
stored and nothing is written.

fresh.description: Fetch again even when the feed has a document already.

format.description: The format it was read as.

keys.description: The keys at the top of the document.

paths.description:
Every path in the document down to a few levels, with `[]` for a
list, each with an example value: the paths `select` takes.

preview.description:
The document, with long lists cut to their first few elements and
long strings shortened, for a person or an agent to read paths from.

selected.description: What `select` picked, when one was given.

value.description: What a binding with this selection would write.

oneOf.description: Words. Escaped for XML, so `&` and `<` show as themselves.
A colour: `#rgb`, `#rrggbb` or `#rrggbbaa`.

FieldValue.description: One field and what it shows now.

default.description:
What it shows when the source's params do not say. For `accent`,
`text` and `panel` the station's brand colours come before this.

fit.description:
The width, in the template's own units, a text holding this field is
shrunk to fit inside. Absent for a field that is never shrunk.

name.description:
The name in `{{name}}` and in `params.fields`: lower case letters,
digits and underscores.

set.description: Whether the source's params set it, rather than a default.

value.description:
What is on screen: the source's own value, the brand colour or the
default, in that order.

Filter.description: One filter in an item's chain.

type.description: The plugin qualified provide id, for example `chroma/filter`.

FilterIdRequest.description: `filter.remove`, and anything else that names one filter.

FilterRecord.description: One filter as the core reports it.

source.description: Absent on a programme filter.

FilterReport.description: A source filter that had to be copied onto each placement.

placements.description: The items it was copied onto, by their path in the document.

code.description: A stable machine readable code, so a client can filter or translate.

detail.description: The numbers behind the message, for a client that draws them.

items.description: The items involved, in the order the message names them.

message.description: One sentence naming the state and the next step.

scene.description: The scene it is in, when it is about one.

Fit.description:
How content fills its frame. SVG's vocabulary, which replaces OBS's seven
bounds types and maps onto `sizing-policy` on a `glvideomixer` pad.

oneOf.description: The content's own size, scaled by `scale`. The frame is ignored.
Fit inside the frame, keeping the aspect ratio.
Fill the frame, keeping the aspect ratio, cropping the overflow.
Fill the frame exactly, distorting the aspect ratio.
Scale so the width matches; the height falls where it falls.
Scale so the height matches; the width falls where it falls.
Like `contain`, but never scale up past the content's own size.

FlatContent.description:
Content on the wire. The same four shapes as the tree, except that a group
names no children: they are records whose parent is the group.

Flush.description: `event/flush`: the end of a batch. A client renders here and not before.

seq.description: The sequence number of the last event in the batch.

Found.description: One thing found on the network.

name.description: The instance name, which is the node's name.

Fps.description: A frame rate as a fraction, so 29.97 is exact.

Frame.description: The rectangle an item is fitted into.

opacity.description: The item's own opacity multiplied by every group's above it.

path.description:
The names from the top item down, so a message can say
`corner / pulpit` rather than an id.

source.description: Present for an item whose content is a source.

source_width.description:
The canvas, which is what the document knows about a source's own size
until the mixer says otherwise. Named so a client that does know can
tell the two apart.

GoLiveRequest.description: `program.golive`: add the page, add the destination, take the page.

id.description: Source id. Derived from the host when omitted.

rtmp.description:
Where to send the programme. Added as an output unless one already
sends there. Omit to leave the outputs alone.

url.description: The page to put on air. Plain http(s); `web+` is added here.

output.description: The output that was created or reused, if one was asked for.

source.description: The source that was created or reused.

state.description: Where the source is now. It goes to programme as soon as it is live.

calibrated_at.description: Unix seconds of the calibration in use; absent before the first.

calibrating.description: True while a calibration is running.

fingerprint.description: The key the calibration is stored under.

ingress_kbps.description:
What arrives: every channel stream and every direct show's input,
as last counted. Zero on a core with no station.

GraphicType.description: One graphic this core can place, as the catalogue has it.

designer.description:
The `[provides.designer]` block, when the plugin wrote one: the icon
for the add gallery, the UI schema, the default frame and the gizmos.

manifest.description: The OGraf manifest's path inside the plugin, so a client can fetch it.

type_id.description:
The plugin qualified id an item's `content.graphic` names,
`ograf/lower-third`.

name.description:
The tray folder to put them in. Null takes them out of the one they
are in.

Header.description:
Everything in the document that is not a scene or an item: the name, the
canvas, the collection's parameters, the transitions it carries, the assets
and the source labels.

It is not a record and it has no id, so it cannot be diffed the way the
tree is. It is carried whole, because it is small and because the
alternative is that a command touching only the header produces an empty
patch and is thrown away by `edit`, which is exactly what used to happen to
`scene.params.set`, `source.set` and `source.group`: all three answered with
the change and none of them kept it.

HeaderChange.description: The header as it was and as it is.

alarms.description: Every alarm that holds now, oldest first.

HealthEvent.description:
`event/health`, from a show that composites, about itself. The station
sends it on to clients as `event/show.health` with the show's id.

HealthState.description: The one word a monitoring wall colours a row by.

oneOf.description: Running and nothing is wrong.

Something is degraded but the picture and sound are going out:
continuity errors or packet loss on the input.

Something a viewer notices, or nothing is going out: no input, a
stall, black, a frozen picture, silence, a failed output, a rendition
the governor refused or shed.
Not monitored: the show is stopped or has no input to watch.

limit.description: How many takes to return, newest first. At most 100.

undo.description: How many steps are still on each stack, so a UI greys out a button.

HlsOutputParams.description: An `hls://` output's params, as an `hls/output` takes them.

Id.description: A UUID in the hyphenated form. Minted ids are version 7 (time ordered); ids derived from a layout are version 8.

add_sources.description:
Add the sources the scenes draw, each through `source.add`. Left out,
only the scenes are added and the answer carries a `[[sources]]` block
in `config_toml` instead.

content.description:
The collection JSON itself, as text: what a page reads from the file
the person picked. Give this or `path`.

path.description:
The collection JSON exported from OBS (Scene Collection, Export), as a
path on the machine the core is running on. Give this or `content`.

config_toml.description:
The `[[sources]]` block for a config file. Only for an import that did
not add the sources itself, which is what the command line wants.

filters_duplicated.description:
OBS attaches a filter to a source, so a camera keyed in one scene is
keyed in all of them. Here filters belong to the item, so a source
filter is copied onto each placement and each copy is named here. This
is the one thing an import changes the meaning of, so it is reported
rather than left for somebody to find on air.

scenes.description: The scenes that were added, by the names they ended up with.

skipped.description: What could not be brought across, and why, one line each.

source_report.description:
Every OBS source and what became of it: carried across, needing a
plugin that is not installed, or skipped with the reason.

sources.description:
The sources the collection needs, by id. Without `add_sources` they
have to be added separately.

sources_added.description: With `add_sources`: the sources added to the mixer, by id.

sources_not_added.description: With `add_sources`: the sources that were not added, each with why.

dry_run.description: Answer with what would change and change nothing. True unless false is sent.

file.description: The project: the object `project.export` answered with, or its text.

machine.description: Also write the file's machine settings: addresses, folders, hardware.

path.description:
The bundle: a `.zip` or the directory it unpacks to, as a path on the
machine the core is running on.

bundle.description: What the bundle said about itself.

missing_plugins.description:
Plugins the collection needs that this core has not got. The scenes
still came across; those items will draw nothing until it does.

relink.description:
Assets that did not come across, with the items that draw them. Empty
when everything landed.

scenes.description: The scenes that were added, by the names they ended up with.

InputSpec.description:
What a show without compositing takes in. A show that composites makes
its input its one source.

backup.description: Switched to when the input stalls, and back when it returns.

params.description:
Per transport: `interface` for multicast, `latency` for SRT,
`passphrase`. Passed to the host as given.

program.description:
The MPEG-TS program of a feed that carries several. Left out: the
first.

InputStats.description: What the input is doing, as the host last counted it.

InstanceRecord.description: One running instance and its cost.

plugin.description:
The plugin it belongs to. Carried on the instance as well as on the
plugin, because `plugin.stats` is a flat list and a caller holding one
row should not have to go back for the name.

enabled.description: Turn a filter off without taking it out.

filter.description: The filter's name, or its position in the item's chain from 0.

ItemProps.description:
An item's props, which is an `Item` with the children lifted out into their
own records.

item.description: The item's name or its id.

type.description:
The item type: a graphic id like `ograf/lower-third`, or a plugin
provide like `camera/source`.

ItemTransition.description: One way on or off the canvas for one item.

duration_ms.description:
How long it takes, in milliseconds. 300 by default, ten seconds at
most.

easing.description: linear, ease-in, ease-out or ease-in-out (the default).

edge.description:
For slide and wipe, the canvas edge it comes in from or goes out to:
left (the default), right, top or bottom.

on_take.description:
Also play it when a scene holding this item is taken, in place of the
scene's own transition for this item.

type.description: cut, fade, slide, zoom or wipe.

edge.description: `align`: left, right, top, bottom, center-x, center-y.

name.description: `group`: what to call the group.

seq.description:
A client's own sequence number, echoed on the patch. See
`SetItemRequest::seq`.

found.description: "point" for the colour at a point, "green" or "blue" for a screen.

share.description: For a screen, the share of the picture it covers, 0 to 1.

id.description: The source id.

screen.description: "green" or "blue" to look for that screen only. Either when left out.

x.description: 0 to 1 across the source's picture. With `y`, the colour there.

KeyMode.description: How a publisher gives its key.

oneOf.description: On the stream name: `main?psk=<key>`, or `key`, `token`, `Token`.
The stream name is the key, for an encoder with one box to type in.

KeyRevealed.description:
What `channel.key.reveal` answers: the key itself, and nothing a list
would carry.

Layout.description: A scene's geometry, for copying onto another one.

scene.description: The scene it came from, for a message.

match.description:
`name` matches item names first and falls back to slot order; `order`
uses slot order alone.

description.description:
What the layout calls its own scene, which is the nearest thing it has
to a description.

params.description: The whole JSON Schema, so a client renders an inspector from it.

sources.description:
The parameters that take a source id, in the order sources are poured
into them.

LayoutItem.description:
One item's geometry: everything about where it sits and nothing about what
it shows.

Limits.description:
The ceilings a client should plan against rather than discover by being
refused.

event_queue.description: How many events the bus holds before a slow client is told to resync.

max_call_secs.description:
Longest any method blocks before it answers. The tightest client
default in the wild, so nothing here can time out a client that used
its own.

max_gain.description:
Loudest a fader can be asked for. Out of range is clamped to this
rather than refused.

max_upload_bytes.description: Largest upload the media endpoint accepts, in bytes.

Listener.description: One listener a channel needs, and whether it is open now.

because.description: The channels it is open for. Empty when nothing needs it.

last_port.description: The last port of a range, for WebRTC media.

loopback.description: Bound to 127.0.0.1 only, so nothing off this machine reaches it.

problem.description: Why it is not open although a channel wants it, and what to do.

protocol.description:
`rtmp`, `rtmps`, `srt`, `whip`, `webrtc` (the media ports WHIP
sessions use) or `relay` (the RTMP port on the loopback alone, for the
mixer's own sources, while no channel has RTMP on).

duration_secs.description:
How long before it goes back down. A minute by default, which is long
enough to reproduce a fault and short enough that a forgotten firehose
stops on its own.

categories.description:
The categories actually raised, which is what the caller asked for
with anything GStreamer does not know dropped.

LogSetRequest.description: `log.set`. Name an instance or a target, not both.

instance.description:
A plugin instance: a source or an output id. Its lines carry the id,
so raising this one raises only that camera.

level.description:
`off`, `error`, `warn`, `info`, `debug`, `trace`, or `default` to stop
overriding this one.

target.description:
A module path prefix such as `godwinmix::mixer`. The longest match
wins, so a more specific override still beats a broader one.

label.description:
What to call the group of changes that follows. Omit it to end the
group, so the next change is its own undo step.

conversion.description:
Where a conversion of this file stands, None when none was asked for in
this process's lifetime.

duration_ms.description:
None when the file could not be inspected; it is still listed, because
an operator would rather see a clip they cannot read the length of than
wonder why it is missing.

faststart.description:
The converted copy's absolute path when one exists on disk. This is
what "add as source" should prefer over `path`.
Whether the moov atom comes first (a player can start before the whole
file arrives). None for a non-ISO container, never a reason to convert
on its own. See `convert::moov_first`.

name.description: Name shown in the UI, relative to the library root.

path.description: Absolute path, which is what gets handed back to the ad break API.

reasons.description: Why it is not, in words an operator can act on. Empty when it is.

video_codec.description:
Short codec name of the first video stream ("h264", "vp9"), None when
there is no video or it could not be inspected.

web_safe.description:
True when the file needs no conversion to play in a browser: H.264 plus
AAC (or no audio) in an MP4. See `convert::web_safety`.

created.description:
True when the folder was not there and this listing made it, so a
client can say "made the media folder" once instead of nothing.

error.description:
Set when the directory itself could not be read, so the UI can say why
the list is empty instead of just showing nothing.

Meters.description:
`event/meters`: the programme bus and every source, in one message at 10
per second, rather than one message per meter as the legacy stream sends.

program.description: Peak dBFS per channel on the programme bus.

sources.description: Peak dBFS per channel, per source id.

MissingRequest.description:
`source.missing`: the ids a scene draws, or none for every source the
mixer knows is not running.

MissingSource.description: One source that is not running, and what would bring it back.

action.description: The button that fixes it, when the error carries one.

error.description: The error it failed with, which names the next step.

restore.description: True when `source.restore` can ask for it again.

type.description: The kind, such as `camera/source`, when the mixer knows it.

MissingWhy.description: Why a source is not running.

oneOf.description: In the mixer, and its pipeline failed. The mixer keeps retrying it.

Asked for (in the config, or by a rebuild) and could not be started.
`error` says why and `source.restore` asks again.
Taken away with `source.remove`. `source.restore` puts it back.

Not in the mixer, and the mixer remembers nothing about it: removed
before the last restart, or never added.

ad.description: Present while an ad break is armed or running.

program.description:
Source currently on program, or None while the slate is showing. A
scene of one full canvas item reports that item's source here too, so
anything written against this before scenes existed still reads.

running_time_ms.description:
Program pipeline running time. Cues are scheduled against this, not
against wall clock, so a client can place a break on a known frame.

scene.description: The scene on air, when one was taken by name.

oneOf.description: The file's sources, outputs, channels and scenes become this mixer's.
Everything in the file is added beside what is here, renamed on a clash.

to_scene.description: The scene it is going to.

fps.description: Frames per second, 1 to 30. The core clamps to what the mosaic runs at.

MultiviewExt.description: `ext.multiview`. Accepts `false` to mean off, or an object.

MultiviewLayout.description: `event/multiview.layout`: how to read the binary frames that follow.

id.description:
Stable for as long as the cells are unchanged, and carried in the
header of every frame, so a client that falls behind can tell which
layout a late frame belongs to.

cells.description:
Cell index to source id, in reading order. Cell 0 is the program return
when it is enabled.

fps.description: Frame rate of the mosaic, so the UI can size its own expectations.

NameRequest.description: `media.convert` and `media.remove` name a file rather than an id.

name.description:
File name as it appears in the media listing. The REST layer puts it
in the path, where the transform rule calls it `id`, so both spellings
are read.

NewKey.description:
A key as it is made, with its secret. Afterwards only an admin gets the
secret again, one key at a time, from `channel.key.reveal`.

secret.description: The key. A list never carries it; `channel.key.reveal` reads it back.

listening.description: Whether this core is listening for nodes at all.

id.description: The node's name, as it was enrolled.

NodeView.description:
What `node.get` reports about one node, and what `node.list` reports about
all of them.

heartbeat_age_ms.description:
Milliseconds since the last heartbeat. The same number
`gmx_node_heartbeat_age_ms` carries.

instances.description: The instances it is hosting right now.

plugins.description: The plugins this node has, name and version.

provides.description: The provide ids this node can run, `<plugin>/<provide>`.

state.description:
`online`, `offline`, or `expected` for a node listed in the config that
has never dialled in.

Ograf.description:
The OGraf manifest, in the subset this host reads.

Everything else the file carries is kept in `rest` and passed on: OGraf is
an EBU specification that will grow, and a key this build has not heard of
is a key a newer client may want. Dropping it here would make the core the
thing that has to be upgraded first.

id.description: The graphic's own id, as the OGraf file gives it.

main.description: The module the web component is in, relative to the manifest.

schema.description:
The JSON Schema of the graphic's own data. What the inspector renders
and what `scene.apply_graphic` fills by name.

stepCount.description: How many steps `playAction` walks through. One means in and out.

rendition_text.description: `copy`, or what the plan gave it, such as `h264 1280x720`.

state.description: waiting, connecting, live, reconnecting, failed, or off.

has_key.description:
False while the address still carries a placeholder a preset wrote in
for somebody to replace, such as `YOUR-STREAM-KEY`. The key itself
never leaves the core, so this is how a client knows to put its own
form up and say "needs a stream key" without ever seeing the key.

True for an address with no key in it at all, an SRT one for instance,
because there is nothing there for anybody to replace.

queue_secs.description:
Seconds of encoded data waiting in the pre-muxer queue. A number that
climbs and stays high means the destination cannot keep up.

rendition.description:
Per kind data from whatever plugin owns this output. Empty for the
RTMP outputs the core builds itself.
What this output asked to be made, when it asked: a rendition
request or a preset. Absent means the programme encoder.

shed.description:
Why the governor has this output's rendition stopped just now, while
it has. The output stays connected and resumes by itself.

Override.description: A sparse change to one item of a referenced scene.

client_seq.description:
The client's own sequence number, echoed back.

A drag cannot wait for a round trip, so the client kit draws the move
itself and reconciles when the echo arrives. Without this it cannot
tell an echo of the move it has already drawn past from a correction,
and the handle rubber bands backwards under the cursor. Every geometry
command carries a `seq`; this is that number coming back.

header.description:
The collection's own properties, when they changed. Absent for the
ordinary case, which is every command that moves an item.

label.description: What the client called this change, for a label in an undo menu.

scope.description:
`document` today. `presence` (who is looking at what) is the other
scope 11 section 4 names and is not implemented.

seq.description:
Monotonic, per core. A client that sees a gap asks for a fresh
snapshot rather than guessing.

source_client.description:
Whoever asked for the change, so a client can suppress the echo of its
own edits and not fight its own optimistic drawing.

name.description: The new folder's name: one folder, no separators, not hidden.

parent.description: The folder to make it in, as `path.list` names it.

PathEntry.description: One folder inside the one listed.

path.description: Absolute, ready to pass back as `path`.

writable.description: Whether the mixer can write into it.

PathExample.description: One path `select` would take, with what it picks.

path.description:
The folder to list. Absent, empty or `~` is the mixer's home folder; a
relative path is taken from there.

dirs.description: The folders in it, sorted by name. Files are never listed.

parent.description: One level up, or null at the top of a root.

path.description: The folder listed, absolute and with links resolved.

truncated.description: True when there were more than 500 and the rest were left out.

writable.description: Whether the mixer can write into this folder.

PathRoot.description: A place the picker may start from.

paused.description: False starts it again. True when absent.

PipelineDot.description:
What `pipeline.dot` answers with on `/rpc`. The REST route serves the same
graph as `text/vnd.graphviz`, so `gmx dot | dot -Tsvg` needs no unwrapping.

dot.description: The graph itself, in the dot language.

PipelineRequest.description:
Which pipeline to look at. A source id, an output id, `programme` or
`multiview`. `pipeline.list` says what is running.

Place.description: Where an instance runs: core, in-process, sidecar, or node:<name>.

PlanNode.description: One node of a plan, as the page draws it.

encoder.description: The catalogue id of the encoder, on an encode node.

id.description: Stable across plans: `encode:programme:h264:1280x720p30:2800k:g2000`.

serves.description:
The outputs it works for, each once (for a channel's plan, the
destination ids), however many rungs of one ladder it serves.

shed.description: Set while the governor has this node stopped to keep what is on air.

PlanReason.description: Why the planner decided what it did.

Playback.description:
The links of an output served as HLS from the control port, each with
the output's viewer key on it.

dash_url_path.description: The same segments as a DASH MPD.

viewers.description: Players that fetched something in the last two windows.

PluginDescription.description: The whole of one plugin, for an agent about to use it.

instances.description: Every running instance of it, with what it costs.

manifest.description: The manifest as JSON, every table of it.

problem.description: Why it is not loaded, when it is not.

provides.description:
The type ids it contributes: what goes in `type` on a source, an output
or a filter.

schemas.description: Per provide id, its settings schema.

skills.description: Per provide id, the description line from its SKILL.md.

source.description: Where it was installed from, as it was typed.

tools.description:
Its MCP tools, as `gmx_<plugin>_<tool>`. Reachable with `search_tools`;
never in the hot list.

trust.description:
What was checked about where this came from: "signed", "signed, digest
only", or "custom, unreviewed". 06 section 4: an operator can only
judge a plugin if the catalogue says what was checked.

plugins_dir.description: Where plugins are read from on this machine.

PluginName.description:
Anything that names one plugin.

The field is `id` because that is what the REST layer fills in from
`/api/v1/plugins/{id}`, and a plugin's id is its name: the namespace of
every id it contributes. `name` is accepted as well, for a JSON-RPC caller
who wrote the obvious thing.

PluginRecord.description: One plugin as the core reports it.

instances.description: Every running instance of it, with what it costs.

problem.description: Why it is not loaded, when it is not.

provides.description:
The type ids it contributes: what goes in `type` on a source, an output
or a filter.

source.description: Where it was installed from, as it was typed.

tools.description:
Its MCP tools, as `gmx_<plugin>_<tool>`. Reachable with `search_tools`;
never in the hot list.

trust.description:
What was checked about where this came from: "signed", "signed, digest
only", or "custom, unreviewed". 06 section 4: an operator can only
judge a plugin if the catalogue says what was checked.
