Normalised 0 to 1 within the item's own box: (0,0) top left, (0.5,0.5)
centre, (1,1) bottom right.

frame.description:
The rectangle the content is fitted into, in canvas pixels. Absent
means the content's own size, scaled.

position.description: Canvas pixels, of the item's anchor point.

Transition2.description: A named transition between two scenes.

TransitionCatalogue.description: `program.transitions`: every transition a take may name on this core.

default_duration_ms.description: What a name on its own runs for, in milliseconds.

easings.description: The four easings every transition takes as `params.easing`.

edges.description: The edges an item transition takes.

item_transitions.description: What an item's `enter` and `exit` may be.

max_duration_ms.description: The longest a transition may run, in milliseconds.

duration_ms.description: The duration a collection stores with it.

origin.description:
`built-in`, `collection` (a named transition the scene collection
stores) or `plugin`.

params.description: The params it reads, for a built in one.

type.description:
The type underneath a collection's name, which is the name itself for
the other two.

TransitionRequest.description: How a take gets there. See docs/reference/transitions.md.

duration_ms.description: How long it takes. 0 is a cut.

params.description: direction, easing, colour, clip... See list_transitions.

type.description: fade, wipe, slide, push, zoom, dip... See list_transitions.

UiDefaults.description:
What a surface starts with: the layout, the theme and the gallery mode.

Chosen by a preset (`preset.apply`), carried in `core.info` and pushed as
`event/ui.changed`. None of it changes what the core does. It exists so the
first page a volunteer sees is the one their preset chose rather than the
one the last person to use this browser chose. 05 section 3b is where the
four gallery modes are defined.

gallery.description:
`live`, `snapshot`, `icon` or `label`. Absent means the surface asks
the machine, which is what `gmx doctor` proposes.

layout.description: Slot to panels, top to bottom. Empty means the surface's own default.

preset.description: The preset that set these, so a surface knows one has been applied.

theme.description: A theme id the surface resolves, for example `dark` or `calm`.

Update.description: One record as it was and as it is.

source.description:
Where the new build comes from. Defaults to wherever this plugin was
installed from last time.

scene.description: Leave it out to check the whole collection.

ok.description: True when there is nothing to fix.

Vec2.description: A point or a pair of factors.

oneOf.description: Anything the decoders know that has no name here yet. Never produced.

VideoShape.description: A picture as it is: codec, size, rate, bitrate.

bitrate_kbps.description: Measured or configured. 0 when unknown (a raw source).

VideoWant.description: The video an output wants. Every field left out is taken from the source.

bitrate_kbps.description:
Target bitrate. A copy is kept when the source is within
`bitrate_tolerance` of it.

bitrate_tolerance.description:
Fraction either way a source's bitrate may differ and still be copied.
0.25 when left out.

keyframe_ms.description: Keyframe interval. Renditions in one ladder share it.

VitalsConfig.description:
`[vitals]`, and what `vitals.set` changes: the thresholds, and whether
to keep a mosaic up for the picture alarms while nobody is looking.

black_luma.description:
An 8 bit luma at or under which a pixel counts as black. 38 is ten
percent of the way from video black (16) to white (235), the figure
ffmpeg's blackdetect uses.

black_ratio.description: The share of pixels that must be black for the picture to be.

black_secs.description: Seconds a picture must stay black before `black` is raised. 0: off.

cc_errors.description: Continuity errors within `window_secs` that raise `cc-errors`. 0: off.

freeze_diff.description:
The mean luma difference between two samples, 0 to 1, under which the
picture counts as unchanged.

freeze_secs.description: Seconds a picture must stay unchanged before `freeze` is raised. 0: off.

loss.description: Packets lost within `window_secs` that raise `loss`. 0: off.

silence_db.description: The peak level in dBFS under which the sound counts as quiet.

silence_secs.description: Seconds the sound must stay quiet before `silence` is raised. 0: off.

stall_secs.description: Seconds without a single packet of input before `stall` is raised.

window_secs.description: The window the two counters are judged over.

actions.does: config.set with that one value; a restart follows when applies is restart
plugin.add with the name as the source
show that part of the client
the same call again, after the wait
setup.start with that piece, then the same call again once it is ready
nothing to call: show the command with a copy button

description: The GodwinMix control protocol. One set of methods, events and types, whether the peer is a UI on /rpc, curl on /api/v1, the CLI, the MCP server or a plugin on stdio.

envelope.description: Keys accepted on every method, handled before a method runs.

confirm.description: The confirm_token from a -32020 refusal, valid 30 seconds. Only a token whose policy is confirm = required needs it.

dry_run.description: On any destructive method. Answers the diff it would make and would_change, against the live state, and changes nothing.

idempotency_key.description: On any mutating method. The answer is kept for 24 hours; a replay returns it with replayed: true. The same key with different params is -32602 with data.idempotency = mismatch.

trace_id.description: Carried into the answer, the X-Trace-Id header and the log line. Taken from the W3C traceparent header over HTTP, or generated.

errors.meaning: the envelope was not a JSON-RPC request
the params were wrong for this method
the core failed while handling the call
not in a state that allows this
the plugin did not declare that placement
the plugin died during the call
a protocol line was over 4 MiB
the change needs the instance restarted
a confirm token is needed first

events.name: event/snapshot
events.summary: The full state, and the sequence number it is current as of. Sent on subscribe and after any change the deltas cannot describe.

events.name: event/program.took
events.summary: The programme changed. Carries the running time the cut landed on, so a client can see how close a scheduled take was to its mark.

events.name: event/scene.patch

client_seq.description: The client's own sequence number, from the `seq` on the command, so a drag discards echoes of moves it has already drawn past.

source_client.description: Who asked for the change, so a client suppresses the echo of its own edits.

events.summary: One change to the scene document, as records rather than a snapshot: what was added, what changed with its before and after, and what was removed. One per transaction, batched and ended by event/flush.

events.name: event/preview.changed
events.summary: A scene was armed, or the arming was cleared. The armed scene is the preview, and program.take with no argument takes it.

events.name: event/source.state
events.summary: A source moved between connecting, live, stalled and failed.

events.name: event/source.position
events.summary: How far through a seekable source has got, a few times a second. Never sent for a camera, which has no position to report.

events.name: event/output.state
events.summary: A destination connected, dropped or is retrying.

events.name: event/adbreak.changed
events.summary: An ad break was armed, went on air, or ended.

events.name: event/ui.changed
events.summary: The surface defaults changed: a preset was applied, or an operator set the layout, theme or gallery mode by hand. Nothing on air moves.

events.name: event/hook.blocked

hook.description: The hook name, for example take.before.

plugin.description: The plugin that owns it, or the URL or command when it came from [[hooks]] in the config.

reason.description: What went wrong and what to do about it.

events.summary: A hook did not get its say: it did not answer inside its timeout, or the thing behind it could not be reached. Whatever the hook was attached to went ahead anyway, which is the rule that keeps a slow hook off the frame path. See 03 section 8.

events.name: event/media.changed
events.summary: A file in the library was uploaded, deleted, or its conversion moved on.

events.name: event/channel.changed
events.summary: A channel changed: made, renamed, switched on or off, a key made or taken back, a stream went live, learned its codecs or left. Carries the whole channel, keys as hints only.

events.name: event/channel.removed
events.summary: A channel was removed. Its publishers were turned away and its keys forgotten.

events.name: event/channel.refused

id.description: The channel, or the application name asked for when no channel has it.

stream.description: The stream name asked for. Empty when the name was the key.

events.summary: A publisher was turned away: no key, a wrong key, a channel switched off, or a name somebody else is already publishing. why is the sentence the encoder was sent. A key is never in it.

events.name: event/meters
events.summary: Peak dBFS for the programme bus and every source, in one message at 10 per second. Replaces the two separate meter events on /ws.

events.name: event/tally
events.summary: Which sources are on programme, on preview, or off. Derived by the core so a Stream Deck does not have to.

events.name: event/alert
events.summary: Something an operator should see. Also written to the log and to the alert webhook.

events.name: event/telemetry

black.description: fraction of the picture at or below black, 0 to 1

lufs_s.description: short term loudness over three seconds, approximated from the programme meter

shot.description: how much the picture changed since the last frame, 0 to 1

sources.description: source id to 1 when it is live and 0 otherwise

events.summary: Numbers instead of a picture, up to ten times a second and under 200 bytes: the shot change score, the black ratio, a freeze flag, short term and integrated loudness, a silence flag and which sources are live. From cheap probes on the raw programme frames, which run only while a client is subscribed.

events.name: event/agent.state

payload.description: The concise agent.state document, plus `why` (one of program, black, freeze, silence, shot) and `snapshot`.

events.summary: The agent.state document, pushed when a telemetry threshold crosses or a take lands, with `why` naming which and a snapshot URL beside it. Edge triggered and at most one a second, so a picture that stays black is one message rather than one a tick.

events.name: event/multiview.layout
events.summary: How to read the binary frames that follow: the cells, and the layout id carried in every frame header.

events.name: event/multiview.frame

payload.description: 16 byte header then JPEG. Not a JSON message.

events.summary: A mosaic frame, as a binary WebSocket frame rather than JSON: a 16 byte little endian header (seq u32, layout id u32, programme running time in milliseconds u64) then the JPEG. The top bit of seq is the stream and is clear on a mosaic frame; the other 31 bits count.

events.name: event/preview.frame

payload.description: 16 byte header then JPEG. Not a JSON message.

events.summary: The armed scene as a picture, on the same socket and in the same 16 byte header as a mosaic frame, with the top bit of seq set to say so and the layout id zero because there is no grid to cut up. One picture per frame: draw it whole.

events.name: event/setup.changed
events.summary: A piece the mixer sets up on first use moved on: the browser renderer or a first party plugin started setting up, got further through its download, became ready or stopped. `message` is for a person; `detail` names paths and commands for a developer.

events.name: event/resync
events.summary: This client fell behind and events were dropped. Re-subscribe for a fresh snapshot; nothing between from_seq and the new snapshot arrives.

events.name: event/flush
events.summary: The end of a batch. Render here and not before, so a client never paints half an update.

events.name: event/rendition.plan
events.summary: The programme's rendition plan changed: an output that asks for a rendition was added, changed or removed, or the governor stopped or brought back an encoder. plan is what rendition.plan answers.

events.name: event/governor.shed
events.summary: The machine ran short while on air and the governor stopped something to keep what is on air whole: what it was and why. It is brought back by itself when there is room again.

events.name: event/show.changed
events.summary: A show was added, renamed, started, stopped, died or came back. Sent by the station to every client, whichever show it is looking at.

events.name: event/show.removed
events.summary: A show was removed. Its process was stopped first.

events.name: event/show.health
events.summary: A show's health changed state, or an alarm began or ended. Never sent for a number alone: read those with show.stats.

events.name: event/feed.failed

binding.description: The binding, when it was a write that failed.

error.description: What went wrong and what to do about it. Never carries a header value.

id.description: The feed.

events.summary: A feed could not be read (a refused connection, a timeout, a body that would not parse, a response over 4 MB), or one of its bindings could not write what it read. `binding` names the binding when it was the write. Sent on the first failure in a row, not on every retry; what was last written stays on air.

events.name: event/feed.recovered

binding.description: The binding, when it was a write that failed.

id.description: The feed.

events.summary: A feed or a binding that was failing works again. `failures` is how many attempts in a row failed before this one.

events.name: event/health
events.summary: This show's health changed: its state (ok, warning, alarm, off) or the kinds of its alarms, never a number alone. From a show that composites; the station sends it on to every client as show.health with the show's id. docs/reference/show-health.md says what each alarm watches.

ext.turns_on: the mosaic pipeline, built on the first subscriber and stopped on the last, plus event/multiview.layout and the binary frames
per source thumbnails from a node

event/preview.frame: the armed scene, composited in the multiview pipeline from the per source thumbnails and published on this socket, to /mjpeg/preview, to scene.preview.frame and to its own cell on the mosaic. "full" composites it at the canvas's own size while a client is subscribed, so a designer's handles land on real coordinates

filter.description: A green or blue screen key with spill removal, a soft edge and a garbage matte
The person cut out of the camera, with no green screen: a matting model on the GPU where there is one and the CPU where there is not

output.description: FLV over RTMP or RTMPS, the ingest every CDN takes
MPEG-TS over SRT, in caller or listener mode
MPEG-TS over RIST (Simple Profile), to a receiver that listens
Record the encoded programme to a new MP4 or Matroska file
HLS and LL-HLS served from the control port, one rung or an ABR ladder
WebRTC playback of the programme or a rendition, served from the control port as WHEP

source.description: An RTMP or RTMPS publisher, decoded with the hardware the machine has
A continuous stream: HLS, DASH, RTSP, SRT, RIST, RTP or UDP
A finite clip on disk or over HTTP, scrubbable, ending with EOS

alpha.description: Whether the clip's transparency is kept. `auto` (or left out) keeps it when the file has it; `false` draws the clip flat through the compositor like any other source.

source.description: A still picture held on screen, or a numbered sequence of pictures played as video

alpha.description: Whether the picture's transparency is kept. `auto` (or left out) keeps it when the file has it; `false` draws the picture flat through the compositor like any other source.

fps.description: Pictures a second for a numbered sequence such as frames/%04d.png. 1 to 120, 25 when left out.

source.description: A command whose process writes a container to stdout
A web page rendered as a live source, by the sidecar or by wpesrc
A web page drawn over the video it was playing, decoded here rather than in the browser
A test pattern and a tone, for the conformance harness
Words on screen, in a box or on their own, rendered once and held with no browser

Align.description: How lines sit against each other and against the box.

Valign.description: Where the words sit up and down in a box taller than they are.

background.description:
A box behind the words: a colour with optional alpha
(`#000000b3`), or empty for no box.

font.description:
A font family installed on the mixer, such as `Sans`, `Serif` or
`DejaVu Sans`. A name the machine does not have falls back to its
default sans serif.

height.description: Height of the box in pixels. Left out, it is as tall as the lines.

outline.description: A colour for an outline round each letter, or empty for none.

padding.description: Space between the words and the edge of the box, in pixels.

radius.description: Corner radius of the box, in pixels.

shadow.description: A soft dark shadow under the letters.

size.description: Height of the letters in canvas pixels, at the item's own size.

text.description:
The words. A new line in them is a new line on screen. Left out, the
part of the address after `text:` is used.

width.description:
Width of the box in pixels at the item's own size. Left out, the box
is as wide as the longest line; given, lines wrap to fit inside it.

source.description: A crawl of words across a bar, or credits rolling up, rendered once and moved each frame

Align.description: How lines sit against each other and against the box.

Valign.description: Where the words sit up and down in a box taller than they are.

oneOf.description: Right to left, a news crawl.
Left to right.
Bottom to top, credits.

background.description:
A box behind the words: a colour with optional alpha
(`#000000b3`), or empty for no box.

font.description:
A font family installed on the mixer, such as `Sans`, `Serif` or
`DejaVu Sans`. A name the machine does not have falls back to its
default sans serif.

items.description:
The items, shown one after another with `separator` between them.
Rolling up, each item is a line.

loop.description:
Go round again for ever. Off, the words cross once and the bar
empties.

outline.description: A colour for an outline round each letter, or empty for none.

padding.description: Space between the words and the edge of the box, in pixels.

radius.description: Corner radius of the box, in pixels.

separator.description:
What goes between items, and between the end of the list and its
start again.

shadow.description: A soft dark shadow under the letters.

size.description: Height of the letters in canvas pixels, at the item's own size.

text.description:
One item, for a ticker of a single message. Ignored when `items` is
given. Left out too, the part of the address after `ticker:` is used.

width.description:
Width of the bar at the item's own size, in pixels. The scene's box
is what it is drawn in; this is only its shape before it is placed.

source.description: A designed graphic: an SVG with named fields, drawn once per change with no browser

fields.description: The template's field values by name, such as {"headline": "Polls close at ten"}. A field left out shows the station's brand colour (accent, text, panel) or the template's default. Change one on air with source.set and params.fields.<name>; template.list and template.fields name every field.

methods.name: adbreak.end
methods.summary: Cut a running ad short, or disarm one that is scheduled.

methods.name: adbreak.start
methods.summary: Interrupt the programme with a clip, then rejoin live when it ends.

methods.name: agent.state
methods.summary: The compact document written for agents: the programme, each source's state and a motion score saying how much its picture is changing.

methods.name: channel.add
methods.summary: Make a channel and its first key, which is in this answer. channel.key.reveal reads it again later.

methods.name: channel.certificate.generate
methods.summary: Make a self signed certificate for RTMPS, for this machine's addresses unless names are given. Encoders must be told to accept it; one from a certificate authority needs no such step.

methods.name: channel.certificate.set
methods.summary: Give RTMPS a certificate: the PEM of the certificate (and its chain) and of its private key, as a certificate authority issued them. Checked before it is kept; the key is sealed and never read back.

methods.name: channel.destination.add
methods.summary: Send a channel's stream on to YouTube, Facebook, Twitch, an RTMP server or an SRT receiver as it arrives. Nothing is decoded or encoded. The key is write only.

methods.name: channel.destination.remove
methods.summary: Stop sending a channel's stream to one destination and forget it. The publisher and the other destinations are not touched.

methods.name: channel.destination.set
methods.summary: Change one of a channel's destinations, naming only what moves: a new key, another server, which stream it sends, on or off. A key left out is kept.

methods.name: channel.get
methods.summary: One channel.

methods.name: channel.key.add
methods.summary: Make another key for a channel, to give to one more person or encoder. The key is in this answer, and channel.key.reveal reads it again later.

methods.name: channel.key.remove
methods.summary: Take one key back. A publisher on air with it is cut off and the next one is turned away; the other keys are untouched.

methods.name: channel.key.reveal
methods.summary: Read one key of a channel back, to give it to an encoder again. Admin only; a list shows only the last four characters. Each read is logged with who asked, never with the key.

methods.name: channel.list
methods.summary: Every channel with its keys (as hints), the address to publish to over each protocol it has on, and what is live on it; and which ingest ports are open and for which channels.

methods.name: channel.remove
methods.summary: Remove a channel and forget its keys. Sources it made that no scene holds go with it.

methods.name: channel.set
methods.summary: Rename a channel, switch it on or off, or change its application name, whether its streams become sources, how its key is given, which protocols it takes (rtmp, srt, whip) or RTMPS and its port. A port opens when the first channel needs it and closes when the last one stops. Only what is named moves.

methods.name: codec.list
methods.summary: Every codec and element in the catalogue, which of them this machine actually has, and what it would pick.

methods.name: config.get
methods.summary: The mixer's settings: each key's value in the config file, its default, when a change to it takes effect, and which keys are waiting for a restart. Secrets say only whether one is set.

methods.name: config.reset
methods.summary: Put settings back to their defaults by taking them out of the config file. Answers like config.set.

methods.name: config.schema
methods.summary: Every setting config.set takes, as one JSON Schema: type, title, description, default, range or choices, and x-gmx-applies (live, next_source or restart).

methods.name: config.set
methods.summary: Change settings in the config file, keeping its comments. Every value is checked first and nothing is written unless all of them fit. Live keys take effect at once; the answer says which wait for the next source or a restart.

methods.name: core.api
methods.summary: Every method, event and type as JSON Schema. The same document as protocol.json and `godwinmix --api-info`.

methods.name: core.doctor
methods.summary: The environment checks: GStreamer, the elements, the config, the disk and the ports. The same list `gmx doctor` prints.

methods.name: core.info
methods.summary: What this core is, what it can do, and where its edges are.

methods.name: core.restart
methods.summary: Stop the mixer and have it started again, when something will start it again. On a supervised core (core.info restart.possible) it answers restarting: true and exits; the programme is off air until it is back. On a core started by hand it answers restarting: false, says how to restart it, and keeps running.

methods.name: core.session_log
methods.summary: The append only record of everything that happened, back as far as you ask.

methods.name: core.shutdown
methods.summary: Stop the mixer, and with it the programme. Nothing else takes the show off air, so this is deliberately its own call.

methods.name: core.startup_report
methods.summary: How long each stage of the start took, and what was over the 250 ms mark.

methods.name: core.status
methods.summary: The full state: programme, every source, every output, the multiview grid, the encoder backend and any ad break.

methods.name: core.subscribe
methods.summary: Subscribe to the event stream. WebSocket only: the core answers event/snapshot then deltas, ending every batch with event/flush.

methods.name: device.discover
methods.summary: Ask every device plugin what it can see: cameras, NDI senders, publishers. Each candidate's params are ready for source.add.

methods.name: feed.add
methods.summary: Add a live data feed: an http(s) address polled every `interval_s` (5 s at least, 30 by default, honouring ETag and Last-Modified), a ws(s) address whose messages are read as they come, or an http(s) event stream with format sse. Header values are sealed.

methods.name: feed.binding.add
methods.summary: Bind a value in a feed to a target: a source's param by path (`params.text`, `params.items`, `params.fields.headline`), a graphic's field through its update action, or a scene parameter. It writes at once if the feed has been read, and after that only when the value changes.

methods.name: feed.binding.pause
methods.summary: Stop a binding writing, or start it again with paused false. Started again, it writes what the feed holds now.

methods.name: feed.binding.remove
methods.summary: Forget a binding. What it wrote stays on air.

methods.name: feed.binding.set
methods.summary: Change a binding's selection or target. Only what is named changes, and the value is written again at once.

methods.name: feed.list
methods.summary: Every live data feed with its state (ok, failing with the reason, paused), when it was last read and last changed, and every binding with the value it last wrote.

methods.name: feed.pause
methods.summary: Stop reading a feed, or start it again with paused false. While paused nothing is fetched and nothing is written; what was written stays on air.

methods.name: feed.refresh
methods.summary: Fetch a polled feed now rather than at the end of its interval. A pushed feed that is waiting to reconnect tries at once.

methods.name: feed.remove
methods.summary: Stop and forget a feed, its sealed headers and every binding that reads it. What they wrote stays on air until something else changes it.

methods.name: feed.set
methods.summary: Change a feed's address, format, interval, timeout or headers. Only what is named changes; a header value of "__secret__" keeps the stored one.

methods.name: feed.test
methods.summary: Fetch a feed once and show what came back: its top keys, a cut down copy, and every path with an example. With `select` (and `template`, `limit`, `join`) it also shows what that picks and what a binding would write. A path that picks nothing is refused with where it stopped and the keys there. Nothing is stored and nothing is written.

methods.name: filter.add
methods.summary: Hang a filter on one source or on the programme, live.

methods.name: filter.list
methods.summary: Every filter in place, with what it is and where it sits.

methods.name: filter.remove
methods.summary: Take a filter out of the pipeline.

methods.name: filter.set
methods.summary: Change a filter's settings in place. A filter that cannot take the change while running says so rather than being restarted behind your back.

methods.name: governor.calibrate
methods.summary: Measure this machine's encoders again, in the background, a few seconds of every core. Refused while anything is on air unless `confirm` is true.

methods.name: governor.status
methods.summary: The resource governor: when this machine was measured, what is in use and free on the CPU and each GPU encoder, and what was shed to keep the programme whole.

methods.name: log.gst
methods.summary: Raise GStreamer's own debug categories for a while, then let them fall back on their own.

methods.name: log.levels
methods.summary: Every log level override in force, and the GStreamer categories still raised.

methods.name: log.set
methods.summary: Change one instance's or one module's log level while the mixer runs.

methods.name: media.convert
methods.summary: Transcode a library file to a web safe copy, in the background.

methods.name: media.list
methods.summary: The clips in the library, with durations and whether each has audio.

methods.name: media.remove
methods.summary: Delete a library file and its converted copy. Refused while it is a live source.

methods.name: media.upload
methods.summary: Stream a file into the library. HTTP only: the body is the file.

methods.name: node.discover
methods.summary: Look for nodes on the local network over mDNS. A network without multicast finds nothing and the [nodes] table in the config is the way there.

methods.name: node.enrol
methods.summary: Mint a one time enrolment token for a node. The answer carries the command to run on the other machine. The token is good for one enrolment and expires.

methods.name: node.get
methods.summary: One node: its clock offset, how long since its last heartbeat, the plugins it has, and the instances it is hosting.

methods.name: node.list
methods.summary: Every node this core knows about: the ones connected now, the ones that have gone quiet, and the ones the config expects that have never dialled in.

methods.name: node.remove
methods.summary: Forget a node. Its bridge is closed, every token minted for a plugin on it is revoked, and its certificate stops working. Sources placed on it go to the slate until they are moved or the node enrols again.

methods.name: output.add
methods.summary: Send the programme to another destination. The encoder is shared, so adding one costs nothing on air.

methods.name: output.get
methods.summary: One destination.

methods.name: output.list
methods.summary: Every destination, with its state, reconnect count and how much is buffered.

methods.name: output.reconnect
methods.summary: Drop and re-establish one destination's connection now, without waiting for its reconnect policy.

methods.name: output.remove
methods.summary: Stop sending to a destination and forget it. Other outputs are unaffected.

methods.name: output.set
methods.summary: Change a destination in place: a new address with a new stream key, a new reconnect policy, a deeper outage buffer. The address is write only, so a client that only wants the buffer never has to hold the key.

methods.name: path.create
methods.summary: Make one new folder inside a folder path.list shows, and list it. A folder that is already there is listed rather than refused.

methods.name: path.list
methods.summary: The folders in one folder on the mixer, and whether each is writable, for a folder picker. Only the home folder and the mixer's own folders are shown; files never are.

methods.name: pipeline.clock
methods.summary: The clock every pipeline is running against, and how far each one has got.

methods.name: pipeline.dot
methods.summary: One pipeline as a graphviz graph: every element, every pad and the caps negotiated between them.

methods.name: pipeline.latency
methods.summary: How much delay one pipeline is carrying, and which stage put it there.

methods.name: pipeline.list
methods.summary: Every pipeline running right now, by the name the other pipeline methods accept.

methods.name: pipeline.queues
methods.summary: Every queue in one pipeline with how full it is, fullest first. A queue that stays full is where the trouble is.

methods.name: plugin.add
methods.summary: Install a plugin, while live, from any source form: a GitHub release (owner/repo), a git URL, cargo:, npm:, pypi:, a local directory, or a bare name looked up in the marketplaces this mixer knows. The signature and the api level are checked before anything is copied.

methods.name: plugin.describe
methods.summary: One plugin in full: its manifest, the settings schema of every provide, and the description from each SKILL.md.

methods.name: plugin.disable
methods.summary: Turn a plugin off without uninstalling it. It registers nothing and runs no process until it is enabled again.

methods.name: plugin.enable
methods.summary: Turn a plugin back on. It registers what it declares and its instances start.

methods.name: plugin.list
methods.summary: Every plugin installed, with what it provides and what each running instance is costing in cpu, memory, latency, dropped buffers and restarts.

methods.name: plugin.reload
methods.summary: Read a plugin's directory again and swap its running instances one at a time, with the freeze frame covering each.

methods.name: plugin.remove
methods.summary: Uninstall a plugin and unwind everything it registered: its provides, its tools, its panels, its hooks and its discovery matchers.

methods.name: plugin.search
methods.summary: Search every marketplace this mixer knows for a plugin, by name, description or kind. Answers what `gmx plugin add <name>` would install.

methods.name: plugin.settings.get
methods.summary: A plugin's settings as they stand, with its schema beside them.

methods.name: plugin.settings.set
methods.summary: Change a plugin's settings. A plugin that cannot take a change while running says so rather than being restarted behind your back.

methods.name: plugin.stats
methods.summary: Per instance cpu, memory, media latency, dropped buffers and restarts, refreshed once a second.

methods.name: plugin.update
methods.summary: Fetch a newer build of a plugin, install it beside the one that is running, and prove it starts. A build that does not answer `initialize` within ten seconds is rolled back and the plugin that was working stays working.

methods.name: preset.apply
methods.summary: Put a preset on this core: its config, its scenes, its layout, its theme and its gallery mode. Pass dry_run to get the plan and write nothing.

methods.name: preset.list
methods.summary: Every preset this core can apply: the six built in, plus anything installed beside the binary or under ~/.godwinmix/presets.

methods.name: preset.save
methods.summary: Turn this core's working setup into a preset directory somebody else can apply. Stream keys and the control token are replaced with placeholders.

methods.name: preview.close
methods.summary: Give up a raw frame socket. The socket goes when the last holder closes it.

methods.name: preview.open
methods.summary: Open a raw frame socket on this machine for a source or the programme, and answer with its path. No encode anywhere: a client on the same host reads the frames the mixer already has. Close it with preview.close.

methods.name: program.get
methods.summary: What is on air, the programme running time, and what revert would go back to.

methods.name: program.golive
methods.summary: One call to put a web page on air: add the page, add the destination, and take the page as soon as it renders.

methods.name: program.history
methods.summary: The last hundred takes, newest first, with the token that asked for each.

methods.name: program.revert
methods.summary: Take back to the shot before this one.

methods.name: program.take
methods.summary: Put a scene or a source on programme. The cut is instant and the outgoing stream is not disturbed.

methods.name: program.thumbnail
methods.summary: What is on air as a small JPEG in base64, {jpeg, width, height, at_ms}, or {pending: true} while the first picture is on its way. An ask keeps one picture a second coming for ten seconds; nothing runs between asks.

methods.name: program.transitions
methods.summary: Every transition a take may name on this core, with the params each reads, and what an item's enter and exit may be.

methods.name: project.export
methods.summary: This mixer as one project file: settings, sources, outputs and renditions, channels, scenes, the page's layout, and its clips by name and size. Keys only with include_secrets.

methods.name: project.import
methods.summary: Open a project file: answers with what it would change (dry_run is true unless false is sent), then replaces this mixer's setup or merges beside it. Says which settings wait for a restart.

methods.name: rendition.plan
methods.summary: What the planner built for every output that asked for a rendition: each node, what it serves, which encoder and why, and the totals.

methods.name: rendition.presets
methods.summary: Every rendition preset, priced on this machine by the governor. One this machine cannot make says so, with why.

methods.name: scene.add
methods.summary: Make an empty scene, or one built from a set of sources.

methods.name: scene.apply_graphic
methods.summary: Fill a graphic that is on a scene, by field name, and optionally play it on or take it off. Answers with the records and, if asked, a still.

methods.name: scene.apply_layout
methods.summary: Apply a layout, making a scene or reshaping one that exists. Applying onto an existing scene keeps the item ids, so the change is a ramp and not a cut.

methods.name: scene.create_from
methods.summary: A scene from a set of sources, laid out by the built in layout for that count (full, two-box, three-box, quad, then a grid) or by a named one. Pictures from the media library become sources, and a keyed layout such as virtual-set guesses its key colour from the camera.

methods.name: scene.duplicate
methods.summary: A copy of a scene with new ids throughout, so editing the copy cannot touch the original.

methods.name: scene.edit.apply
methods.summary: Write a draft back into the live document.

methods.name: scene.edit.begin
methods.summary: Take a working copy of a scene. Editing is off air by default: the draft is written back on the next take of that scene, or when you apply it.

methods.name: scene.edit.discard
methods.summary: Throw a draft away. The live document is untouched.

methods.name: scene.export
methods.summary: The whole collection: as JSON, or as a zip bundle carrying its assets with a hash each, which is what you send somebody.

methods.name: scene.get
methods.summary: One scene: its records and where every item actually lands on the canvas.

methods.name: scene.graphic.list
methods.summary: Every graphic template this core can place, with what each one takes.

methods.name: scene.history.mark
methods.summary: Group the changes that follow into one undo step, until the next mark. This is what makes a drag of forty moves one Ctrl+Z.

methods.name: scene.import
methods.summary: Read a collection bundle, a zip or the directory it unpacks to, and add its scenes to this one. Answers with a relink report for any asset that did not come across.

methods.name: scene.import.obs
methods.summary: Read an OBS Studio scene collection and add its scenes to this one. Send the file's text as `content` (what a page's file picker reads) or a `path` on the mixer's machine. With `add_sources: true` the sources the scenes draw are added through source.add, and the answer says which were added and why any were not.

methods.name: scene.item.add
methods.summary: Put something on a scene's canvas. With no transform it lands in the next free cell, so a drop never needs a dialog.

methods.name: scene.item.align
methods.summary: Line items up on an edge: left, right, top, bottom, center-x or center-y.

methods.name: scene.item.arrange_grid
methods.summary: Lay items out in a grid of `cols` columns.

methods.name: scene.item.bind
methods.summary: Bind a geometry property to an expression over the collection's parameters, so changing a number moves everything that follows it.

methods.name: scene.item.copy
methods.summary: Copy an item into another scene. The copy keeps the transform and the filters and gets a new id.

methods.name: scene.item.cover_canvas
methods.summary: Put items over the whole canvas, filling it and letting the overflow go.

methods.name: scene.item.distribute
methods.summary: Space items evenly between the two on the ends, horizontally or vertically.

methods.name: scene.item.filter.add
methods.summary: Hang a filter on one item, so a camera keyed in one scene is not keyed in all of them.

methods.name: scene.item.filter.remove
methods.summary: Take a filter off an item.

methods.name: scene.item.filter.set
methods.summary: Change one of an item's filters, or turn it off without taking it out.

methods.name: scene.item.fit_to_canvas
methods.summary: Put items over the whole canvas, keeping their aspect ratio inside it.

methods.name: scene.item.group
methods.summary: Put items into a group. The picture does not change.

methods.name: scene.item.match_size
methods.summary: Make items the same size as another one.

methods.name: scene.item.move
methods.summary: Move an item to another scene, keeping its transform and filters.

methods.name: scene.item.remove
methods.summary: Take an item off a scene.

methods.name: scene.item.reorder
methods.summary: Move an item up or down the stack, between two named neighbours.

methods.name: scene.item.schema
methods.summary: What one item type takes: a graphic's OGraf schema, or a source or filter plugin's settings schema. The same JSON Schema every client renders an inspector from.

methods.name: scene.item.set
methods.summary: Assign an item's properties. Only the keys named move; the rest are left alone, so calling it twice with the same body changes nothing the second time.

methods.name: scene.item.ungroup
methods.summary: Take a group apart, leaving every child exactly where it looked.

methods.name: scene.layout.copy
methods.summary: Read one scene's geometry, to paste onto another.

methods.name: scene.layout.list
methods.summary: The layouts that ship with the core, with the parameters each one takes.

methods.name: scene.layout.paste
methods.summary: Put one scene's geometry onto another's items, matched by name first and slot order second. Items that match nothing are left alone.

methods.name: scene.list
methods.summary: Every scene in the collection, with how many items it has, the sources it draws and whether it is armed.

methods.name: scene.params.get
methods.summary: The collection's typed parameters, readable without their values, so a client discovers what is fillable before filling it.

methods.name: scene.params.set
methods.summary: Set the collection's parameter values, declaring any that are new. A `{{name}}` in any string property of any item follows them, so one call changes every lower third that uses it.

methods.name: scene.preview.frame
methods.summary: A still of the armed scene as base64 JPEG, the floor every client has.

methods.name: scene.preview.set
methods.summary: Arm a scene. The armed scene is the preview, and program.take with no argument takes it.

methods.name: scene.redo
methods.summary: Put back what undo took away.

methods.name: scene.remove
methods.summary: Delete a scene. What is on air is not touched.

methods.name: scene.rename
methods.summary: Change a scene's name, its colour, or both. Names and colours live on the document, so every client, the tally and an agent see the same ones.

methods.name: scene.transaction.abort
methods.summary: Throw the batch away. The document goes back to where it was when the batch opened.

methods.name: scene.transaction.begin
methods.summary: Start a batch. Everything until the commit applies on one frame or not at all, and undoes in one step.

methods.name: scene.transaction.commit
methods.summary: Apply the batch.

methods.name: scene.undo
methods.summary: Undo the last change. A drag marked with scene.history.mark undoes as one step.

methods.name: scene.validate
methods.summary: Overlaps, items off the canvas, safe area breaches and missing sources: what to fix before saying a scene is done.

methods.name: setup.get
methods.summary: Where one piece stands, without starting anything.

methods.name: setup.list
methods.summary: Where each piece the mixer sets up on first use stands: the browser renderer (`web`) and every first party plugin this copy carries.

methods.name: setup.start
methods.summary: Set a piece up now, or join the set up already running, and answer at once with where it stands. Progress follows as `event/setup.changed`. Sources waiting on the piece start by themselves when it is ready.

methods.name: show.add
methods.summary: Make another show and start it: empty, a copy of a show (without its outputs, so nothing goes out twice), or from a project file.

methods.name: show.add_many
methods.summary: Make many shows in one call, such as every channel of a headend. The whole batch is checked first. With dry_run (the default) nothing is made: the answer says what would be, what its renditions would cost and whether the governor would admit them. Without it, every show that fits is made and the rest are refused with why; a show is made whole or not at all.

methods.name: show.list
methods.summary: Every show on this machine: its name, whether it is running, what is on air, what its outputs send and what its process costs. `current` is the show a client reaches when it names none.

methods.name: show.output.add
methods.summary: Send a show without compositing to another place: an address (SRT, RTMP, UDP, RTP or RIST), a platform and its key, or hls://<name> to serve it as HLS from this port. Left without a rendition it copies the input's bytes; with one it is planned and admitted by the governor. The key is write only.

methods.name: show.output.remove
methods.summary: Stop one output of a show without compositing and forget it, key and all.

methods.name: show.output.set
methods.summary: Change one output of a show without compositing, naming only what moves: another address, a new key, on or off, copy or a rendition.

methods.name: show.remove
methods.summary: Stop a show and remove it with its folder. Refused for the last show and for main, the show the station was started with.

methods.name: show.remove_many
methods.summary: Stop and remove many shows. Each id that cannot go (main, or one not there) is refused with why, and the rest go.

methods.name: show.rename
methods.summary: Give a show another name. Its id stays.

methods.name: show.set
methods.summary: Change a show's name, its input, or whether it composites. Turning compositing on starts a show process whose one source is the input and moves the outputs to it; turning it off hands them back to the direct host, when the show has one source and no scenes in use. A switch can take half a minute, so it answers at once with a task_id and the show as it is; task.get with that id carries this answer, with how long the outputs were off, once it is done.

methods.name: show.start
methods.summary: Start a stopped or failed show.

methods.name: show.stats
methods.summary: Health, input numbers and each output's numbers for many shows in one read, from what the station already holds, so it is cheap to call every second for two hundred shows. `fields` narrows it to health, input or outputs.

methods.name: show.stop
methods.summary: Stop a show. It keeps its config, and stays stopped when the station starts again, until show.start.

methods.name: snapshot.get
methods.summary: One JPEG: the whole contact sheet, the programme, or one source cut out of the mosaic.

methods.name: source.add
methods.summary: Add a source while the mixer runs. Answers with the id it got and the whole source record.

methods.name: source.audio.set
methods.summary: Move a source's audio: the fader, the mute, and for a superimposed page the balance between its own sound and the videos under it.

methods.name: source.duplicate
methods.summary: Add another source like one the mixer has: the same address and settings under a new id. A client cannot do this with source.add, because the address it is shown has everything after the host cut off.

methods.name: source.get
methods.summary: One source. Refused with the ids that exist when there is no such source.

methods.name: source.group
methods.summary: Put sources in a tray folder. A tag for finding things, not a group on the canvas.

methods.name: source.key_color
methods.summary: The colour to key a source on: the colour at a point of its picture, or with no point the green or blue screen it stands in front of.

methods.name: source.list
methods.summary: Every source, with its state, whether it has video and audio, and its fader.

methods.name: source.missing
methods.summary: Sources that are not running, and why: failed, could not be started (with the error and the action that fixes it), removed, or unknown. Pass the ids a scene draws, or none for every one the mixer knows about.

methods.name: source.remove
methods.summary: Remove a source. If it is on programme the mixer cuts to the slate first.

methods.name: source.restart
methods.summary: Build a source's pipeline again now, rather than waiting for its next retry. For a source that could not be started or was removed, use source.restore.

methods.name: source.restore
methods.summary: Put back a source that source.remove took away, as it was: same id, address, settings, fader and mute. The mixer remembers the last sixteen it removed, until it restarts.

methods.name: source.seek
methods.summary: Move a seekable source to a position. Answers with where it actually landed.

methods.name: source.set
methods.summary: Change a running source: its name and colour, its params, or where it runs. The name and colour live on the scene document. Moving a source between the core, a sidecar and a node is `place`; the programme keeps its frame rate across the move and the compositor covers the swap.

methods.name: task.cancel
methods.summary: Ask a piece of long running work to stop. Cooperative: the answer says the request landed, not that the work has stopped yet.

methods.name: task.get
methods.summary: How a piece of long running work is getting on, and its answer once it has one.

methods.name: task.list
methods.summary: Every background job this core knows about, newest first.

methods.name: template.fields
methods.summary: A running graphic's fields: each one's label, type, default and what it shows now.

methods.name: template.get
methods.summary: One template, with its SVG as written.

methods.name: template.list
methods.summary: The graphic templates: the built in pack and the SVG templates in the media library, each with its fields.

methods.name: template.save
methods.summary: Check an SVG template and write it into the media library.

methods.name: tool.call
methods.summary: Call one of a plugin's tools, in MCP's shape. The name is `<plugin>/<tool>`, or the bare tool name when only one plugin has it.

methods.name: vitals.get
methods.summary: This show's health (its state and alarms, null in the first second) and the thresholds they are judged by.

methods.name: vitals.set
methods.summary: Change the alarm thresholds, or whether a mosaic is kept up for the black and freeze checks while nobody is looking. Fields left out keep their defaults; a duration of 0 switches that check off. Applies within a second.
